topPositive.text: You can't beat the price to performance on this tv. No one else is doing 120hz at 4K and still retaining good HDR out of the box. Black levels are really good and HDR pops and isn't overly bright where it's inaccurate. Highly recommend if you've got a PS5/XSX
topPositive.author: Luis

topNegative.text: It arrived with a broken screen. Walmart has received it, but the app says it can take 3 weeks to get a refund. I want to go buy another one in the store, so I can make sure it arrives safely. However, I need the refund 1st! I do not recommend having it delivered. FedEx does not need to be delivering TVs.
topNegative.author: KimberlyO

topPositive.text: TV picture is incredible. Colors are vibrant, blacks are actually black and not that weird pixelated grey. The gaming mode has a bunch of great options and the frame rate is on par with gaming monitors. The picture mode for sports makes everything very clear with no motion blur. The built in sound is also very good as the TV has built in subwoofers. The viewing angle is the only downside, if you are watching from more than a 15° angle the opposite side of the TV looks a little dark.
topPositive.author: Kyle

topNegative.text: The shipment company used is horrible they delivered TV damaged twice now. The box had major visible damage which ended up cracking the screen. Would not recommend buying tv from Walmart given the freight shipping company issue.
topNegative.author: Sarat

topPositive.text: The remote during the set up process was not responsive in many instances.  The tv also turned off 3 times during the process. Additionally I didn't see a barcode to register the tv. It had to be done manually. The chatbots are a waste of time. The tv has a nice picture and sound quality for the price.
topPositive.author: LadyGirl

topNegative.text: What a piece of garbage . The picture is poor the sound constantly crackles and pops. It was shipped upside down and left at my door on its side by FED EX
topNegative.author: CHRISTINA

topPositive.text: OK it's my first Smart TV, it took half a day to get around two things that stomped me first was of tuning off subtitles and second how to get back the folders in my 4TB HDD. So All's great, just love the picture way better than the 18" I've been watching for 16 years.
topPositive.author: Gopher

Good luck getting 5 years out of it.
Heaps of dead pixels only getting worse
topNegative.author: 1 year warranty

topPositive.text:
I recently switched from a Samsung OLED to the LG OLED83C6PSA, and I have to say I'm genuinely impressed.

The picture quality is fantastic. The OLED panel delivers excellent contrast, deep blacks and a really punchy, detailed image without losing the natural look of movies and TV shows. The 83" screen is also incredibly immersive, particularly when watching 4K content.

What has surprised me most is how much I'm enjoying the overall picture compared with my previous Samsung OLED. The LG has a very clean, refined image, and with a few adjustments to the picture settings, I've been able to get exactly the look I like.

The processing is also very good, with smooth motion and excellent upscaling of lower-quality content. The TV feels premium in both picture quality and overall build.

I watch a lot of movies and series, as well as sport, and the C6 handles all of it extremely well. It has only been a short time, but so far I'm very happy with the change and would definitely recommend giving the C6 serious consideration if you're looking for a large-screen OLED.

walmart:15013023340.title: It's not a "TELEVISION" It's an infotainment sys.
walmart:15013023340.text:
It's not a television, it's an industry espionage infotainment system. 
              You'll need to learn basic computer and smartphone technology to use it. 
                                           If you don't have internet access forget it.
     Most of the apps are unavailable without an email subscription, mobile number or access to a computer to verify identity or various accounts by entering codes sent to a mobile device or email. In some cases an app on another device is needed. 
               Because the system makes device and other account associations I have some serious privacy concerns that are too technical to explain in this review.
    The remote is not a remote control in the traditional sense, it's an interface device mainly controlled by voice that limits people with disabilities. There are NO physical controls on the system pannel, if you loose the controller, it breaks, or the batteries fail, you will have no access to the system. This fact requires the purchase of 2 other remotes as backups as soon as possible (before their all gone model no.RC923A) to ensure access for the alleged 30,000 hours of system life should one controller fail or they get lost or eaten by the dog.

walmart:15153350266.title: Great, except for one thing
walmart:15153350266.text:
This TV is basically one of the best things you can get for current gen gaming without getting an OLED. The contrast is insanely good with local contrast (local dimming) and peak brightness maxed out. It  almost makes SDR content LOOK like HDR. It's THAT good. There is one issue I have with it, though. 

At least when gaming, there is noticeable inverse ghosting at all refresh rates from 60hz to the maximum 144hz. If you din't know what that is or what it looks like, think motion blur, but instead of the blur being the same color of the moving object, it's an inverted color instead (like a dark object with white trail behind it and vice versa). This seems to be a problem when dark colors transition to bright colors. 

This is all typically caused by the voltage on the pixels being boosted too much in order to try and increase the response time and reduce sample and hold motion blur. Monitors usually have an option to adjust it (usually called "overdrive") but that is not present here, unfortunately. So unless TCL decide to release a firmware update to give us that option in the game bar menu to disable overdrive (I don't know if they will though), were kinda stuck with it.

I've mostly been able to tune it out, but if that seems bothersome to you, you might want to save up and wait to get an OLED.

walmart:15153350266.title: Strong All-Rounder with a Few HDR
walmart:15153350266.text:
The TCL QM7K is a strong mixed-usage TV. Its high brightness, especially in SDR, makes it a standout in well-lit rooms, handling ambient glare well though struggling with direct light sources. In darker rooms, it delivers fantastic contrast and deep blacks even with bright highlights on screen, despite some noticeable blooming. Colors are vivid but HDR accuracy is off out of the box, so purists may want it calibrated. Solid processing rounds out the package, handling sub-optimal content well.
On the plus side, it offers deep blacks in any lighting, vivid colors (especially in HDR), HDMI 2.1 support with 4K at 144Hz and 1080p at 288Hz plus VRR, and ample SDR brightness for well-lit rooms. The main drawbacks are poor HDR accuracy out of the box and visible glare from direct light sources.

walmart:16035918154.title: Faulty TV and poor warranty support
walmart:16035918154.text:
I purchased a TCL QM8K 75-inch TV in December 2025 after spending months researching and waiting specifically for Black Friday deals. Initially, the TV performed fairly well—good picture quality overall—but I did notice some ghosting during fast-moving scenes like sports (pucks and balls in motion).

By mid-April 2026, the TV completely stopped working. No power at all.

Trying to get support from TCL was frustrating from the start. Their phone system pushed me into automated prompts, and after going through the process multiple times, I was placed on hold and then disconnected—this happened five separate times without ever reaching a person.

I began the warranty process on April 17. After eventually reaching out via email, this led to several days of back-and-forth, including sending videos of the issue. As of today (May 2), this process is still ongoing, and I've now been told it will take an additional 15–20 days just to process the refund once issued.

In the end, TCL offered a refund for the original purchase price instead of a replacement.

The problem is that this doesn't actually make the situation whole. I had carefully chosen this TV based on months of research and timing around sale pricing. Now that those deals are gone, the refund doesn't allow me to purchase an equivalent model. TCL also stated they had no comparable stock available and declined to offer any form of compensation beyond the original price.

Their response included the line: “Please rest assured that your case is being handled in accordance with warranty guidelines.” That may be true—but it highlights the real issue.

Before buying from TCL, it's worth asking yourself whether you're comfortable with how their warranty process works. If your TV fails within a few months, you may end up starting your search all over again at a higher cost, waiting weeks for resolution, and handling disposal of a broken unit yourself.

walmart:16035918154.title: Solid TV, would buy again.
walmart:16035918154.text:
Originally ordered via Best Buy but rescheduled  my delivery the day before it was scheduled to be delivered, so I looked around to see what other retailers might have it in stock. Walmart showed delivery in two days and came through, with a better price than Best Buy. 

The television itself is great quality. It is MiniLED, so it gets bright and the local dimming makes shows and movies pop. It's good for multiple uses. I use mine connected to an Apple TV for streaming and I also have a PC connected for general use and gaming. It's low latency and works well for gaming. I have played everything from RPG to FPS and they all run extremely well. 

I would recommend adjusting the picture settings to the recommendations from RTINGS. They do a really great job with in-depth reviews on build and picture quality and I have been using their recommendations for years. 

On picture quality, my primary point of reference is an LG C2 OLED. I think the picture quality is more or less equal. The OLED has *zero* blooming (the light bleed around bright objects on dark background) and MiniLED can occasionally have a little on logos and things like that but it's definitely not distracting and the difference is brightness more than makes up for that to me. 

The sound is good for a TV but really almost any sound bar will sound better. I think the best use for TV speakers is for pairing with a soundbar from the same maker to add effect and layers to the soundbar. 

Overall it's a great tv and I would buy another. I saw some of the TVs TCL released at CES2026 and I'm still quite happy with my choice, especially the value and I would recommend this tv throughout the year until maybe Black Friday when the new (2026) TVs come down to reasonable prices.

Oh, disable all the tracking items, wifi and bluetooth and use an Apple TV or similar.

walmart:16104452413.title: Horrible delivery, $300 price swap, and subpar tv.
walmart:16104452413.text:
Hisense and Walmart.com, not Walmart stores, and Estes Express Delivery dropped the ball on this television all the way around.  First, Walmart.com had the price at $1298.99 and then changed it while is was in my cart to $1598.00.  I should have cancelled the order then, but I wanted to have the 5 year warranty.  Then, they used Estes Express Lines, and the driver left the tv in the street, against a light pole right before it started raining.  I'm disabled, so I had to get my wife to come home from work to help my daughter bring it inside.  Then, the base had to be cracked open, per instructions, to install the base onto the television.  Once we got everything hooked up, it had an update that continually failed on wifi and ethernet.  I did everything that online tutorials and Hisense requested me to do, including purchasing a 32GB flashdrive to download it via USB.  That also failed.  I reset the tv 5 times trying to download the update.  The streaming services continually glitched, The sound kept on fluctuating.  The supposed great sound from the television was tinny and anemic for all the extra surround speakers and woofers it had.  Next, the picture was really great, and I had it at the right brightness for my dimly lit livong room, but then an ad came on with a white screen, and it increased in brightness to its full capacity, blinding my wife and I temporarily.  I tried for three days to accomplish the update, I tried for three days to fix the brightness.  I contacted Hisense, and their service department was helpful in that they were willing to send a tech out to see if it was repairable, but two things, the instructions about the service on a brand new tv wanted me to send a picture of every angle of the television in case the tech damaged the television, and then, as I was looking at options for a different television in case it didn't work out, Walmarr.com dropped the price back down to $1298.99, seriously, 3 days later, after I got treated horribly about the issue by an Indian phone center operator. who barely spoke English, and was cometely useless.    Walmart stores can't  even intervene.  These clowns raised the price $299.01 and then dropped it back down three days after I had it in my home.  Thats ok Walmart.com.  It going back.  Sorry Hisense, you had one chance, and while you say this is your flagship model, you really need to work on a different approach for your updates and your build quality.
P.S.  the upper half of the base dropped out of the packing and al.ost cracked out tile floor because someone in their great wisdom didn't think to secure it in the packing but left it to fall from the top when the carboard was taken off.  Also, the whole bottom of the packaging was shredded.

walmart:16104452413.title: BUYER BEWARE . . .
walmart:16104452413.text:
This TV shows a lot of promise out of the box.  I was impressed watching my favorite college football team last Saturday.  However, I was not impressed with Walmart's after-purchase price policies.

I tend to shy away from reviews that stray from reviewing the product, and focus more on the actual buyer experience , i.e. shipping, customer service, yada yada yada.  Still, I would like to share my experience regarding 1) Walmart's Price Match Policy and 2) Walmart's Price Adjustment Policy.

Shortly after my purchase (within 7 days), Walmart online competitors (BestBuy and Amazon) reduced their prices significantly.  I erroneously thought Walmart still price matched.  WRONGO!  Walmart does NOT PRICE MATCH their competitors prices.

Watching the item online, I saw that Walmart did drop the price, though, eventually to $100 LESS than I paid.  I called my local Walmart and was told to come down for a PRICE ADJUSTMENT.  However, once I got to Customer Service, I was nicely informed that I was given incorrect information.  Walmart stores cannot adjust prices on ONLINE sales.  Instead, if you are within the return window you can bring the item into the store and RETURN IT for a full refund.  Then, you can REPURCHASE the item ONLINE (or in store) for the reduced price.  That's fine for a coffee maker.  But a 67-pound TV package that's already installed?  Not so much.

I strongly recommend that Walmart ONLINE shoppers compare Walmart Price Policies with their competitors'  online price match and price adjustment policies to receive the best buy possible.

walmart:16347258322.title: The Sony BRAVIA 5 (K-50XR50) is a vibrant, versati
walmart:16347258322.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Alright, I've been living with the Sony BRAVIA 5 (K-50XR50) for a couple of weeks now, and I'm ready to spill the tea on this 50-inch Mini LED TV. Spoiler: it's a solid performer, but it's not without quirks. Let's dive in.

First off, the picture quality is legit impressive for the price. The Mini LED setup with Sony's XR Backlight Master Drive makes colors pop and blacks feel surprisingly deep for an LCD. Watching *Dune: Part Two* on Sony Pictures Core was a treat—those desert scenes had vibrant oranges and crisp details that pulled me right in. The Cognitive Processor XR does some heavy lifting, upscaling older shows like *The Office* so they don't look like a blurry mess. HDR is solid with Dolby Vision, but don't expect OLED-level punch; bright highlights in movies like *Mad Max: Fury Road* can feel a bit flat compared to pricier sets like the BRAVIA 7.

Gaming is where things get a bit mixed. I hooked up my PS5, and the 4K/120Hz support with Auto HDR Tone Mapping is awesome for *Spider-Man 2*—colors and contrast adjust on the fly, which is cool. But the response time isn't the snappiest, so fast-paced games like *Call of Duty* had some noticeable blur. If you're a casual gamer, it's fine, but competitive players might want to look elsewhere.

Sound-wise, the TV holds its own. The 20W speakers with 3D Surround Upscaling create a decent sense of space, and Dolby Atmos makes action scenes feel immersive. I paired it with a Sony soundbar for extra oomph, and the Acoustic Center Sync feature is a game-changer—dialogue feels like it's coming right from the screen. Still, don't expect it to rival a dedicated surround system.

The Google TV interface is slick and snappy, with all the apps I need (Netflix, Disney+, you name it). The BRAVIA Connect app on my phone made setup a breeze, and AirPlay 2 is handy for streaming from my iPhone. My only gripe is the remote—it's functional but feels a bit cheap for a TV this nice.

Design-wise, the Underlay Stand looks sleek and saves space, though it wobbles a tad if you bump the table. It's great for smaller rooms, and the tactile dots on the HDMI ARC port are a thoughtful touch for accessibility. 

Overall, the BRAVIA 5 is a great all-rounder for movies, shows, and casual gaming in a bright room. It's not perfect—HDR brightness could be better, and gamers might want faster response times—but for a mid-range Mini LED, it's tough to beat. If you're after a reliable 50-inch TV that looks and sounds great without breaking the bank, this one's a winner.

walmart:16375305955.title: Bravia 8 ii
walmart:16375305955.text:
The 55” Bravia 8 ii was intended to replace an old 43” plasma tv. I ended up returning the Bravia.

The picture on the Bravia 8 ii is superior…end of story. If I were paid to come up with a problem with the picture the only thing that I could come up with is that the blacks can at times be too black. The satin finish on the screen is awesome and reduces reflections. I am used to less real estate and lower resolution, so the Bravia picture was a huge upgrade.

The Bravia attempted to output PS5 with a 4k cable but was glitching out. The Bravia output PS5 flawlessly with an 8k HDMI cable and it looked fantastic. Bravia played nice with Roku device using 8k HDMI cable.

The audio on the Bravia 8 ii is shockingly poor and the reason that I returned the unit. The human voice on the Bravia is so small and “tinny”. It sounds like a bunch of nano-people stuffed in a can. I literally kept thinking about a Fred Flintstone transistor radio from my childhood. Contrasting the small voices, the background noises are loud and thunderous. It leads to a constant volume battle between the parts of the show without sound effects vs the parts of the show with sound effects. Turn the volume up to try to hear the little canny voices…turn the volume down when the sound effects start up and blast you away. The Bravia has excellent audio settings and even a setting for prioritizing voice. But I just could not get the setting right to compensate for the tinny, canny, little voices.  The settings to increase voice quality only added to the canniness of the sound. I kind of thought that TV audio was all worked out long ago and I have never had a problem with a TV's native audio before, so this was really a big surprise to me. Ultimately, I decided that at this price point, I need to be able to actually hear the voices rather than to keep struggling trying to fix something that is not fixable.

For my hands the remote control provided with the Bravia 8 ii is too small physically, too slippery, and the buttons are too flush to the body housing to be easily detectible. I bought a universal remote to try but ended up returning the Bravia before seeing if the 3rd party remote would work on the Bravia.

This TV is probably a good pick for the crowd that likes to augment the audio with sound bars or theater sound systems. You cannot go wrong with the picture for sure. For the crowd that just want a TV to sound like a TV, maybe not such a good pick.

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been using the Sony Bravia 55-inch for a while now, and I can confidently say it's a solid upgrade if you care about both picture quality and smart functionality. It's also pretty lightweight for a 55” TV, which made wall mounting straightforward. It looks sleek and modern in my space without feeling bulky.

One small thing to note: if you're sensitive to glare, the screen does reflect a bit in brighter rooms, so some strategic placement or curtains can help.

Overall, I'm really happy with this TV. It hits a great balance between high-end features and price. Definitely a worthy addition if you're upgrading your home entertainment setup.

walmart:16998272236.title: Something I don't like
walmart:16998272236.text:
I’ve been using the LG B5 65-inch OLED for about three months, and while it nails some things brilliantly, it also leaves me frustrated in areas that matter for daily use.

Picture Quality

The standout feature. Honestly, the best picture quality I’ve ever seen, especially considering this is LG’s entry-level OLED.

Colors are vibrant, contrast is excellent, and black levels are deep. Movies and gaming look stunning.


Sound

Surprisingly loud and clear for built-in TV speakers. Good enough for casual use without a soundbar.


UI & System Behavior

WebOS is laggy, cluttered, and lacks basic controls like aspect ratio/zoom.

TruMotion introduces ugly artifacts in fast horizontal pans—turned it off completely.

The AI features feel gimmicky and pointless.

Major annoyance: when resuming from rest mode, the TV doesn’t remember what I was watching. It always defaults to HDMI (in my case, PS5).

Bluetooth connectivity with my Bose Soundlink Mini is unreliable. Volume control often breaks, forcing me to reset/reconnect.


Remote Control

Honestly terrible. No dedicated play/pause button for OTT apps.

The scroll wheel is clunky, inaccurate, and unfortunately the primary button. Makes navigation more frustrating than it should be.


Other Notes

Installation took an absurdly long time (a full week after delivery).

Price feels a little steep considering the buggy UI and weak smart features. The hardware is amazing, but the software drags it down.


Verdict
If you’re buying purely for picture quality, the B5 is a winner. But if you care about a smooth smart TV experience, responsive UI, or a decent remote, be prepared for disappointment. I hope LG takes software updates seriously, because the potential here is huge but wasted by poor execution.

I do further research and find that this has been a problem for years, with people begging for another option and LG ignoring them. For a premium OLED TV, that is honestly unacceptable, the TV should be easy to use out of the box and not feel like it is actively fighting against you as you try to navigate content and settings.

It may be a solvable issue using third party hardware, but due to the fact that the TV is very annoying and difficult to use without additional purchases and doesn’t give a tiny toggle in the settings to disable “magic pointer” forever (while loading up the TV with bloat and software that the user will never want to use, such as an AI chatbot), I am not able to give this TV higher than one star. walmart:19695456161.title: Impressive picture and sound quality
walmart:19695456161.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been enjoying the TCL QM7L for several weeks now and I'm impressed! Everything from classic cinema to live sports looks fantastic on this screen. My TV room is quite bright, and the vivid colors and 4K resolution stand up to the challenge. Darker-leaning content is a little harder to view during the daytime because the screen has a glossy and reflective finish, which creates some minor distractions. This has always been the case for my set up, so the issue is not specific to this television.

I am new to Google TV and have been loving it. The home screen and apps are very intuitive and easy to navigate.

I'm using a soundbar (which fits underneath the screen when mounted on the stand's higher setting) but I'm impressed by the quality of the built-in Bang & Olufsen sound system. In a smaller room, you could absolutely rely on it as your main audio output.

Additional pros: the backlit remote, the many picture controls for adjusting everything to your exact liking, the fast processing between commands, the TV's auto shut-off feature.

Minor grievances: the TV stand is sloped so my soundbar sits a little awkward on top of it, and I don't love the way the cords are viewable from the side profile (even though they can be tethered through the stand they don't sit flush against the back).

In conclusion, this television is an amazing value for its user experience and picture/sound quality. I am very happy with it and would rate it a 4.8/5.

Overall, this TV vastly exceeded my expectations, and I would highly recommend it to anyone who wants a high quality television without the OLED price point.

walmart:19695456161.title: Superior image quality
walmart:19695456161.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The TV replaced my older 4K TV, which is significantly better in image quality and sound with a few tweaks.

Installation: super easy, 4 screws at the bottom of the stand. Put it flush against the back of the screen and screw in 4 longer screws.
Gently flip the screen upright on a stand. It's easier with two people, but the tv is lightweight enough to be done by one person. Remove the film along all edges.

Image quality: It's 4K and super crisp. Everything looks better than in real life. Foods look so juicy that they look like they are jumping out of the screen.

Image colors: The is where I had to play around with. It accentuated magentas/ reds and turquoise blues. What fixed it for me was to go into Color Space in the display settings and change it from Native to Auto. I also increased Saturation and decreased Color Temperature a bit.

Sound: it has Bang and Olufsen speakers. I played around with the sound but couldn't get what I wanted. It either sounded too brassy or too tinny and overall it sounded like someone was talking into a bucket, especially on high volume settings. On low volume, it sounded really good. But I wanted to be able to listen to music and enjoy the quality of the sound on high volume settings. For that, I bought a generic sound system and it worked great. 

Speed: it turns on super fast, any videos or streams start playing right away. The remote buttons are very responsive and fast.

Apps: coming from an older TV, I had no idea how many free content apps this TV offers: from Google TV platform to on demand movies to live streaming and scheduled broadcasting.

To sum it up: it's a superb upgrade ti a 4K tv that has crisp image quality with a few correctable tweaks, offer plenty of free content apps and it fast and highly responsive.

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] This is my fourth Samsung TV. All have been high-performance and delivered good value. The positives:

I just wanted to turn on the TV and go to cable, but I got a screen full of apps, including a link to HDMI 3, where the cable box sits. Finding the cable system with the TV remote was also challenging. Eventually, I found the settings to go straight to cable, but it took a couple of weeks. I also set up Alexa, but then decided I didn't want it turned on. I couldn't figure out how to disable it on the TV. Fortunately, I could disable it on the Alexa app. My previous Samsung TVs had more picture-setting options. I finally used Expert settings to get what I wanted. Everything is working well now, and it was worth the effort. It's just that the effort to get the TV working the way I wanted took 2-3 weeks. The manual provided very little help. [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My family having the 55" Samsung Neo QN70H TV in our living room completely elevates the daily home entertainment experience. From the moment we turn it on, the display jumps out with vivid colors and striking brightness. Powered by Quantum Mini LED technology and Quantum Dot color, it delivers ultra-sharp contrast, deep blacks, and rich highlights that hold up effortlessly even in sun-drenched rooms.  
​At 55 inches, it strikes the ideal balance for most living spaces—large enough to feel immersive without dominating the room. Under the hood, Samsung's NQ4 AI Processor dynamically upscales lower-resolution media into crisp 4K, making standard streaming shows, movie classics, and live sports look significantly sharper and more detailed.  
​The sleek AirSlim profile gives the display a virtually borderless, modern look whether mounted on a wall or placed on a media stand. Daily usability is just as smooth: the One UI Tizen smart interface makes navigation fast, organizing all your favorite streaming platforms and smart home controls in one central hub. Integrated audio features like OTS Lite and Q-Symphony dynamically match sound to movement on screen, pulling you straight into the action.  
​Ultimately, owning the Samsung QN70H means never settling for average picture quality again. It transforms movie nights, gaming sessions, and casual viewing into a premium theater-like experience right from the comfort of my couch.

walmart:19931816238.title: The best of the best
walmart:19931816238.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After spending time with my new Samsung 65" OLED S90H 4K Vision AI Smart TV, I can confidently say this is one of the most impressive televisions I've ever owned. Samsung has taken OLED performance to another level, combining stunning picture quality with genuinely useful AI-powered features that make everyday viewing more enjoyable.

The first thing that stands out is the incredible brightness. Unlike my previous TVs that I noticed struggled in well-lit rooms, this television delivers a vibrant, punchy image that looks fantastic at any time of day. It's HDR content is breathtaking, with highlights that appear bright and realistic while still maintaining the deep, inky blacks that OLED technology is famous for.

The contrast performance is simply outstanding. Dark scenes reveal exceptional shadow detail while bright elements pop from the screen with remarkable depth. Whether watching blockbuster movies, sports, or nature documentaries, the picture has an almost three-dimensional quality that constantly draws you in.

Another area where my television excels is panel uniformity. My unit exhibits excellent screen consistency, with virtually no distracting banding, dirty screen effect, or noticeable unevenness. Large areas of colour appear smooth and uniform, making sports, gaming, and panoramic scenes look clean and natural.

The TV is also incredibly responsive. Navigation through menus is fast and fluid, apps launch quickly, and gaming performance is exceptional. The combination of Samsung's processing power and the OLED panel results in smooth motion and rapid response times that make everything feel effortless.
One of the biggest surprises I've noticed is that it has been the TV's AI-powered upscaling. The new Vision AI features are where Samsung has really pushed innovation forward. The AI is constantly working behind the scenes to optimise picture and sound settings based on the content being viewed and the environment in the room. The result is a television that feels smart rather than complicated.
Beyond the automatic enhancements, the AI features are genuinely fun to use. Voice interactions feel more natural, content recommendations are more relevant, and the TV can adapt settings without requiring constant adjustments. It's exciting to see the television recognise what you're watching and intelligently enhance the experience in real time. 
Overall, I find this television is an exceptional television that combines stunning OLED picture quality, outstanding brightness, excellent uniformity, class-leading upscaling, and innovative AI capabilities. The result is a TV that not only looks spectacular but also feels like a glimpse into the future of home entertainment. It's a premium viewing experience that consistently impresses every time I switch it on.

I rate this television 5/5 Stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

walmart:19931816238.title: High contrast, visual new experiences
walmart:19931816238.text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I hadn't upgraded the TV in my bedroom for 10 years! So I knew I had a lot to gain when I bought this OLED TV, which has been a dream of mine. Assembling the stand and putting it on my furniture was pretty easy!! I needed just a hand to move it correctly.I did most of it by myself. The screen is very slim. Instantly it has a modern look. Although I can't really see the anti-glare film on the screen , I have already noticed it has less glare than my previous TV.  The set up was easy and it prompted me to download the SmartThings app. There were a few instances where I felt like the operating system was asking for too many privacy permissions.  My phone is a remote control through the SmartThings app and the physical remote control is very responsive and slim. The voice command button on the remote does not work, I don't know why, I did plenty of trouble shooting. The feature works on my phone remote though and I can search things with AI (bixby). A lot of the times it misunderstands me or takes me away from what I want on the TV so I don'rt use the AI search feature unless I am desperate. 
 Installing my apps was easy, but I had to figure out Samsung‘s App Store, which I had never used before. It was straightforward and logging into my apps was easy ‘cause  I can use a QR code.
Now to the TV itself, the picture. The screen is VERY bright so I am very happy with that! In the past when I'm watching my favorite shows that have clandestine sneaky, dark scenes such as basically anything in the Game of Thrones series.On my old TV I couldn't really see what was happening in the dark and that's the reason I wanted to upgrade. This TV is a game changer in terms of the clarity of dark scenes!! When this TV really really blows me away is in high contrast scenes such as tribal council in survivor where you have rich blacks, and then fire. This looks amazing on this Oled screen. Having this clear high contest picture brings me to a new level enjoying drama and my whole family has noticed the difference. Also the TV OS is very fast and it makes a cool old timey blip when I turn the TV off. Overall I am happy with the tv, the picture and sound are both great.

walmart:20031806459.title: PS5 User's Dream: Incredible Performance and Value
walmart:20031806459.text:
This tv has completely exceeded my expectations for gaming. If you are looking for a compact TV that doesn't compromise on next-gen console features, this is the one.
The standout feature for me is the inclusion of four full HDMI 2.1 ports. It is incredibly convenient to have a PS5, soundbar, and any other gear hooked up at the same time without needing to swap cables. With native 4K resolution at a 120Hz refresh rate, gameplay is buttery smooth. Fast-paced action games look amazing thanks to the Variable Refresh Rate and Auto Low Latency Mode, which completely eliminate screen tearing and keep input lag super low.
The exclusive PlayStation 5 features are also a huge plus. The Auto HDR Tone Mapping is flawlessly, making dark shadows and bright highlights look incredibly detailed. Plus, the TV automatically switches into Game Mode when I turn on my console, so I never have to fiddle with the settings before jumping into a match.

The picture is as crisp as you can get. Anything 4K or animated is clean and detailed. I've watched sports, cartoons, and regular shows and they all look excellent. The sound is amazing, even with a ceiling fan on high and the volume on 25/100.  I can see the light reflected from the ceiling fan on the TV but that's the only glare I can see other than the programming. 
The TV links to the app seamlessly for control without the remote control. The pre-installed apps work just as well as the ones I run from my device.  All in all, a great purchase thus far.

walmart:20446824532.title: TV whole new level of color and brightness
walmart:20446824532.text:
I have been using LG TVs for many years and have always been very satisfied with them. Recently, during our move, our previous TV was accidentally damaged. Because of the great experience and positive impression I had with LG TVs, I decided to purchase the new 86QNED86 and 65QNED86 models for our living room and bedroom respectively.

The very first thing I noticed after installing them was the bright and crystal clear picture quality. Our living room gets a lot of natural light, and with our previous TV, the screen sometimes felt dull during the daytime. However, the QNED86 delivers outstanding brightness, making the picture look sharp and vibrant even during the day.

I mainly watch sports, YouTube, and Netflix, and LG's signature clean and vivid picture quality really enhances the viewing experience and immersion. In addition, the WebOS system is fast, intuitive, and extremely convenient to use.

The sound quality was also better than expected, and the design is sleek and beautiful, matching perfectly with the rest of our furniture and home interior.

As always, I highly recommend LG TVs.

walmart:20446824532.title: Cinema-Level Picture at Home!!
walmart:20446824532.text:
This TV completely transformed my living room into a luxury cinema experience. The first time I turned it on, I genuinely sat there for an hour just replaying nature videos because the colours and detail looked unreal. The Mini LED display is on another level — bright highlights sparkle beautifully, dark scenes stay rich and detailed, and every colour feels incredibly lifelike without looking artificial.

Movies feel cinematic, sports look unbelievably smooth, and gaming on this screen is addictive. Fast motion stays crystal clear, and the immersion is incredible with the huge vibrant display and deep contrast. Even older content somehow looks refreshed and sharper.

What surprised me most is how premium everything feels. The design is elegant and modern with ultra-thin bezels, so the screen almost disappears into the room. The smart interface is fast, intuitive, and packed with features that actually make daily use enjoyable instead of frustrating.

The sound quality also deserves praise — powerful, clear, and immersive enough that I didn't feel an immediate need for a soundbar. Dolby Atmos content especially sounds fantastic.

LG absolutely nailed the balance between cutting-edge technology and everyday usability with this model. It looks expensive, performs like a flagship, and makes every movie night feel special. Easily one of the most impressive TVs I've ever owned and worth every dollar.

Just got this LG 65-inch QNED and I'm really happy with it so far. The picture quality looks great, colours are nice and vibrant, and everything feels really sharp, especially when watching 4K stuff.

It's also bright enough to watch comfortably during the day, which was important for me. The design is clean and modern, so it fits well in the living room without looking too bulky.

Overall, feels like a solid buy for the price. Definitely worth it if you're looking for a good 65-inch TV.
